I remember an issue I was involved in that was trying to determine the "costs" of competing proposals for disposal of heavy industrial plating waste streams. The most costly required each stream generator to treat its waste on site. Other proposals allowed transportation of the wastes in tankers to an aggregated site for "pounding". While this presented enhanced economies of scale, the mixing of the wastes complicated their treatment processing and increased costs. The "cheapest" was a plan to dilute the waste with sewage effluent and pump it into the ocean. Just tap into the outfall and drip, drip, drip.
